question.text: Vindhya Event-Driven Fund buys an INR 1,000 face-value corporate bond (8% annual coupon, annual pay) 120 days after the last coupon date at a clean price of INR 1,010. Using 365-day basis, what is the dirty (invoice) price paid?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under standard bond settlement conventions, the buyer pays the dirty (invoice) price, which is the clean price plus accrued interest since the last coupon date. Accrued interest = Face × Coupon × (Days / Day-count basis) = 1,000 × 0.08 × (120 / 365) ≈ INR 26.30. Dirty price = Clean price + Accrued interest = 1,010 + 26.30 = INR 1,026.30. The Trap: INR 1,010 is the clean price and omits accrued interest. INR 1,090 adds a full year's coupon instead of pro-rating for 120 days. INR 1,050 uses 180 days, which is not given. Note: The clean-price-plus-accrued-interest dirty-price formula, the 365-day basis, and the specific INR 1,026.30 calculation are not explicitly set out in the cited XIX-E (Category III AIF Managers) workbook pages, which contain general valuation and accrued-interest concepts. The bond-pricing convention applied above reflects general industry/market practice for fixed-income settlement.
